title: HYDRAULIC STEERING-CYLINDER & BRACKET
summary: Power steering (N40) power cylinder (ram) under the front of the car: the cylinder's ball stud bolts into the relay rod (center link) with a castle nut and cotter pin, and its rod end passes through a bracket hung from the frame, cushioned by grommets, retainers and a spacer and held by a nut and cotter pin. The bracket bolts onto two studs that belong to a reinforcement inside the frame rail (no separate studs).

parts.name: CYLINDER ASM.
parts.name_expanded: Power steering cylinder (power cylinder / ram) assembly

parts.name: REINF. ASM.
parts.name_expanded: Reinforcement assembly – frame, with two studs for the cylinder bracket

parts.name: BRACKET
parts.name_expanded: Bracket – power cylinder rod to frame

parts.name: RELAY & TIE ROD ASM.
parts.name_expanded: Relay rod (center link) & tie rod assembly

materials.where: relay rod ball joint at the left of the drawing

fastening.note: Reinforcement [2] sits inside the frame rail with two studs (part of [2], no separate callout) pointing down through the frame; bracket [11] goes on the studs and is held by lock washers [3] and nuts [4].

Cylinder rod end passes through bracket [11]: retainer [7] and grommet [8] on the inner side, spacer [10] on the rod through the bracket, then grommet [8], retainer [7], nut [6] and cotter pin [5] on the outer side.
Cylinder ball stud end goes into the relay rod [12] from above; nut [14] with cotter pin [13] underneath.

View A: the cylinder's clamp on the relay rod is centered 1/2 ± 1/16 from the end of the rod; position LH inner clamp with slot downward ±10° rearward & forward. The clamp is part of the relay/tie rod assembly (no callout).
Rivet [9] drops into a hole in the end of the relay rod at the arm; its purpose is not shown.
Relay & tie rod assembly [12] attaches to the arm with attaching parts listed in UPC 9 (not on this sheet).
